sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 NPR 的《Hidden Brain》。我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: When Eitan Hirsch was growing up, newspapers were a central part of the family's daily routine.
sentences.zh: Eitan Hirsch 在成长过程中，报纸是他们家日常生活的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: If you were a member of the household, you kept up with the news.
sentences.zh: 如果你是这个家庭的一员，你就得跟上新闻动态。

sentences.en: My parents raised me and my siblings in a politically engaged environment.
sentences.zh: 我的父母在一种热衷政治的环境中抚养我和我的兄弟姐妹长大。

sentences.en: You know, we always were, we knew what was going on in the news.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们一直都是这样，我们了解新闻里正在发生什么。

sentences.en: The newspaper was delivered to our home.
After Eitan went off to college, his father kept reading, listening to the radio, staying up to speed.
sentences.zh: Eitan 上大学离开家后，他父亲依然坚持阅读、收听广播，保持对时事的了解。

sentences.en: And then, a few years ago, Eitan learned that his dad had developed a new habit.
sentences.zh: 然后，几年前，Eitan 发现他父亲养成了一个新习惯。

sentences.en: He would lie on his bed at night and watch cable news.
sentences.zh: 他晚上会躺在床上看有线电视新闻。

sentences.en: Out front next, breaking news, Trump's tantrum, a jaw-drapping...
sentences.zh: 接下来是前线报道，突发新闻，特朗普的暴怒，令人瞠目结舌的……

sentences.en: Eitan, now a political scientist, found this puzzling.
sentences.zh: 如今已是政治学家的 Eitan 觉得这很费解。

sentences.en: I've never really personally, like, gotten into cable news.
sentences.zh: 我个人从来没有真正迷上过有线电视新闻。

sentences.en: This has never been something I've enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 这从来都不是我喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: I asked him why I was doing it, and he said, you know, it's our duty to be informed.
sentences.zh: 我问他为什么要这么做，他说，你知道，了解时事是我们的义务。

sentences.en: And I said to him, you know, but you already are informed.
sentences.zh: 我对他说，可是你已经了解了呀。

sentences.en: You know, you've already read the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你已经读过报纸了。

sentences.en: You've already listened to all the radio.
sentences.zh: 你已经听过所有的广播了。

sentences.en: What possibly more could you be getting from this?
sentences.zh: 你还能从这里得到什么额外的信息吗？

sentences.en: I think in the end, it was pretty clear that he just likes politics.
sentences.zh: 我想归根结底，很明显他只是喜欢政治。

sentences.en: A lot of people like politics.
And to decompress at night, you know, more than the Food Network, the Kardashians, whatever else is on TV,
sentences.zh: 而且为了在晚上放松心情，比起美食频道、卡戴珊家族或者电视上播放的其他节目，
他更喜欢看有线电视新闻。

sentences.en: Millions of Americans are like Eitan's dad.
sentences.zh: 数百万美国人就像 Eitan 的父亲一样。

sentences.en: They eagerly follow television personalities and the ups and downs of the latest scandal in Washington.
sentences.zh: 他们热切地关注着电视名人和华盛顿最新丑闻的起起伏伏。

sentences.en: Nearly a month after the House passed too late...
sentences.zh: 在众议院通过（法案）近一个月后，太晚了……

sentences.en: It's just a week since the Rouser TV star Kim Kardashian West visited the president in Washington.
sentences.zh: 距离真人秀明星 Kim Kardashian West 访问华盛顿总统府才过去一周。

sentences.en: They know who testified last week on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 他们知道上周谁在国会山作证。

sentences.en: Tense moments in the room between Democrats and Republicans.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和共和党人在会议室里气氛紧张。

sentences.en: If this is not impeachable conduct, what is?
sentences.zh: 如果这都不算弹劾理由，那什么才算？

sentences.en: And what the rumor mills are saying about who's in and who's out at the White House.
sentences.zh: 还有流言蜚语在传白宫里谁得势、谁失宠。

sentences.en: National Security Advisor Michael Flynn has resigned after less than a month.
sentences.zh: 国家安全顾问 Michael Flynn 在任职不到一个月后辞职。

sentences.en: Bannon is officially out at the White House.
John Bolton is out of the government.
Gentlemen, I have to jump in here.
I love this debate here, but we have to go to a short break.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这里的辩论，但我们必须先休息一下。

sentences.en: After that short break, we'll continue our discussion on still more Washington scandals.
sentences.zh: 短暂休息后，我们将继续讨论更多华盛顿丑闻。

sentences.en: If you ask them why they follow the news so closely, they will tell you what Eitan's father told him.
sentences.zh: 如果你问他们为什么如此密切关注新闻，他们会告诉你 Eitan 父亲告诉他的理由。

sentences.en: It's an act of civic virtue to stay informed.
sentences.zh: 保持知情是一种公民美德。

sentences.en: Eitan Hirsch is skeptical, and he has the data to prove it.
sentences.zh: Eitan Hirsch 持怀疑态度，并且他有数据来证明这一点。

sentences.en: He argues, provocatively, that what his dad is doing isn't really about politics or policy or elections.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一个挑衅性的观点：他父亲所做的这些，其实与政治、政策或选举无关。

sentences.en: It's really just about his dad.
sentences.zh: 这其实只是关于他父亲自己。

sentences.en: It seemed to me that the way that people are doing politics is much more similar to a hobby
sentences.zh: 在我看来，人们参与政治的方式更像是一种爱好，

sentences.en: than to what I think of a politics, which is acquiring power.
sentences.zh: 而不是我所理解的政治——即获取权力。

sentences.en: Today we look at a strange twist of modern politics in the United States.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来看看美国现代政治中一个奇怪的转折。

sentences.en: We live in a 24-7 cycle of political news that saturates every corner of our culture.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个 24 小时全天候的政治新闻周期中，它渗透到了我们文化的每一个角落。

sentences.en: It seems like this has led to increased engagement in politics.
sentences.zh: 这似乎导致了人们对政治参与度的提高。

sentences.en: But Eitan Hirsch says that engagement with politics, for many of us,
sentences.zh: 但 Eitan Hirsch 说，对于我们许多人来说，这种对政治的参与，
实际上已经变得更加肤浅了。

sentences.en: As a result, he says, our democracy, from the workings of city government to the battle for the presidency,
sentences.zh: 他说，结果就是，我们的民主，从城市政府的运作到总统职位的争夺，

sentences.en: is increasingly distant from the actual needs of citizens.
sentences.zh: 正日益远离公民的实际需求。

sentences.en: The paradox of our passion for politics, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》，探讨我们对政治热情的悖论。

sentences.en: Eitan Hirsch is a political scientist at Tufts University.
sentences.zh: Eitan Hirsch 是塔夫茨大学的政治学家。

sentences.en: He studies voting, elections, and how we participate in politics.
sentences.zh: 他研究投票、选举以及我们如何参与政治。

sentences.en: In his book, Politics is for Power,
sentences.zh: 在他的书《政治是为了权力》中，

sentences.en: Eitan makes the case that millions of Americans are engaging in politics
sentences.zh: Eitan 指出，数百万美国人参与政治的方式，

sentences.en: in ways that are emotionally satisfying, but ultimately self-defeating.
sentences.zh: 虽然在情感上令人满足，但最终却是自挫的。

sentences.en: They're there to serve their own emotional and intellectual needs.
sentences.zh: 他们参与是为了满足自己的情感和智力需求。

sentences.en: They're not trying to move anyone.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是想去改变任何人。

sentences.en: They're not trying to empower anything.
sentences.zh: 他们也不是想去推动任何事情。

sentences.en: They're really just trying to learn and engage in a pretty frivolous way.
sentences.zh: 他们真的只是在以一种相当轻浮的方式学习和参与。

sentences.en: So I would imagine that a lot of people listening to you would disagree with your assessment of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，很多听你节目的人会不同意你对他们的评价。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people would say,
I derive no entertainment from the shenanigans of the Republicans or the intransigence of the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我从共和党人的胡闹或民主党人的顽固中得不到任何娱乐。

sentences.en: In fact, I feel exhausted and dispirited by the state of our politics all the time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我一直对我们政治的现状感到筋疲力尽和沮丧。

sentences.en: Some people probably would agree that, yeah, you know,
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会同意，是的，你知道，

sentences.en: being on Twitter all the time or sharing a meme about some silly news story is entertainment.
sentences.zh: 整天刷 Twitter 或分享关于某个愚蠢新闻故事的表情包确实是一种娱乐。

sentences.en: But the feelings that they bring to politics are much deeper.
sentences.zh: 但他们带入政治的情感要深刻得多。

sentences.en: They care and they feel hurt that politics isn't going the way they want it.
sentences.zh: 他们在乎，并且因为政治没有按照他们希望的方向发展而感到受伤。

sentences.en: And they feel joy when politics does go the way they want it.
sentences.zh: 当政治如他们所愿时，他们会感到快乐。

sentences.en: The thing is that what they're actually doing is not participating themselves in any active way.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，他们实际上并没有以任何积极的方式参与其中。

sentences.en: They're really just following the news.
sentences.zh: 他们真的只是在关注新闻。

sentences.en: They're following the ups and downs of a presidential primary cycle or the Mueller report or the impeachment hearings.
sentences.zh: 他们关注着总统初选周期、穆勒报告或弹劾听证会的起起伏伏。

sentences.en: And so they themselves are not participating.
sentences.zh: 所以他们自己并没有参与其中。

sentences.en: You introduced a word that I hadn't actually heard in the context of politics.
sentences.zh: 你引入了一个我在政治语境下从未听过的词。

sentences.en: You said that people are really pursuing a hobby.
sentences.zh: 你说人们实际上是在追求一种爱好。

sentences.en: They're in it for the fields, the thrill of debates, scoring points.
sentences.zh: 他们沉浸其中是为了那种感觉、辩论的快感和得分的乐趣。

sentences.en: And you call these people hobbyists.
sentences.zh: 你把这些人称为“政治票友”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by the term?
Yeah, so, you know, I was kind of reading through some of the sociology literature on hobbies.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我当时读了一些关于爱好的社会学文献。

sentences.en: They're things that are people doing either to, you know, they're learning facts.
sentences.zh: 它们是人们为了学习事实而做的事情，你知道，

sentences.en: They learn facts about birds, whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 他们学习关于鸟类的事实，随他们喜欢。

sentences.en: Or they're engaging in collecting materials.
sentences.zh: 或者他们从事收集材料。

sentences.en: Or they're, you know, engaged in kind of crafts.
sentences.zh: 或者他们，你知道，从事某种手工制作。

sentences.en: And it seemed to me that the way that people are doing politics is much more similar to a hobby than to what I think of a politics, which is, you know, acquiring power.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，人们参与政治的方式更像是一种爱好，而不是我所理解的政治，即获取权力。

sentences.en: So they will learn a lot of facts and talk about those facts.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会学习很多事实，并谈论这些事实。

sentences.en: They will participate in a kind of craft.
sentences.zh: 他们会参与某种“手工”活动。

sentences.en: Like they'll go online and share memes, have a discussion.
sentences.zh: 比如他们会上网分享表情包，进行讨论。

sentences.en: Very similar to how sports fans, you know, listen to sports radio.
sentences.zh: 这和体育迷收听体育广播非常相似，你知道。

sentences.en: They'll talk about the gossip of, you know, what this quarterback or that quarterback is doing.
sentences.zh: 他们会谈论这个四分卫或那个四分卫在做什么的八卦。

sentences.en: And that's sort of the end of it.
In politics, I think that's exactly what people are doing, too.
sentences.zh: 我认为在政治上，人们做的也正是这些。

sentences.en: If we define political participation as a form of engagement where you are trying to move public policy or electoral politics in a direction you care about, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果我们把政治参与定义为一种试图推动公共政策或选举政治朝着你关心的方向发展的参与方式，你知道，

sentences.en: you have your one vote and you're convincing another person to vote the way you want or to advocate the way you want.
sentences.zh: 你投下你的一票，并说服另一个人按照你想要的方式投票，或者按照你想要的方式去倡导。

sentences.en: That really doesn't describe the behavior of what most people are doing when they're doing politics.
sentences.zh: 这并不能描述大多数人在从事政治活动时的行为。

sentences.en: It looks much more like what they're doing is similar to a sports fanatic engaged in sports or a foodie watching food shows, reading restaurant reviews.
sentences.zh: 这看起来更像是体育迷沉迷于体育运动，或者美食家观看美食节目、阅读餐厅评论。

sentences.en: It seems much more in that category of life than in the category of power acquisition.
sentences.zh: 这似乎更属于那一类生活方式，而不是权力获取的范畴。

sentences.en: So when I think about a hobby or I think about being a sports fan, I think about people who derive, you know, great satisfaction or great frustration from what's happening.
sentences.zh: 所以当我想到爱好或体育迷时，我想到的是那些从发生的事情中获得巨大满足感或巨大挫败感的人。

sentences.en: They engage in it passionately, but ultimately they'd have to acknowledge that their involvement has little consequence.
sentences.zh: 他们充满激情地投入其中，但最终他们不得不承认，他们的参与几乎没有什么后果。

sentences.en: If they wanted to actually participate in politics seriously, they would go about this all differently.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想真正认真地参与政治，他们会以完全不同的方式去做。

sentences.en: Instead of hating the other side, instead of hating a random person who says they're a Republican or says they're a Democrat, they would say, hmm,
sentences.zh: 他们不会去憎恨另一方，不会去憎恨一个自称共和党人或民主党人的普通人，而是会想，嗯，

sentences.en: is this a neighbor that I can convince to move in my direction?
sentences.zh: 这是一个我可以尝试说服并让他转向我这一边的邻居吗？

sentences.en: And when we talk to organizers who are out every day in the trenches trying to convince other people to come along with them, they don't hate the other side.
sentences.zh: 当我们与那些每天都在一线努力说服他人加入他们的组织者交谈时，他们并不憎恨另一方。

sentences.en: It's like totally the wrong frame of reference for them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这完全是错误的参照系。

sentences.en: They're thinking about how do I move a person?
sentences.zh: 他们在思考：我该如何去影响一个人？

sentences.en: There might be a person on the other side who says they're a Republican and I'm a Democrat or says they're a Democrat and I'm a Republican.
sentences.zh: 对方可能有一个人自称是共和党人，而我是民主党人，或者自称是民主党人，而我是共和党人。

sentences.en: And my first reaction is, oh, they believe all these things I think are despicable.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是，哦，他们相信所有我眼中卑劣的东西。

sentences.en: But my second reaction, if I really care about moving them, is what do they care about that I care about that I can leverage to move them in my direction?
sentences.zh: 但我的第二反应，如果我真的在乎去影响他们，就是：他们关心什么是我也关心的，我可以利用这一点来引导他们转向我这一边？

sentences.en: And in sports fandom and in the kind of shallow way that people engaged in partisan fandom, that second step is never made.
sentences.zh: 而在体育迷文化和人们参与党派迷文化的肤浅方式中，那第二步永远不会迈出。

sentences.en: There's never a goal to convince a Yankee fan to come to the Red Sox.
sentences.zh: 从来没有一个目标是去说服洋基队的球迷转投红袜队。

sentences.en: And if you're online or, you know, only talking about politics to people who are exactly like you,
sentences.zh: 如果你在网上，或者，你知道，只和那些和你完全一样的人谈论政治，

sentences.en: there's no point of thinking of a person on the other political party as someone you need to convince of anything.
sentences.zh: 那么把对方政党的人视为你需要说服的对象就毫无意义了。

sentences.en: You don't need to convince them of anything because you're not doing anything.
sentences.zh: 你不需要说服他们任何事情，因为你根本什么都没做。

sentences.en: And if you're a Red Sox fan, of course, you are deriving satisfaction precisely from the camaraderie you have with like-minded people,
sentences.zh: 如果你是红袜队的球迷，当然，你正是从与志同道合的人之间的情谊中获得满足感，

sentences.en: as opposed to reaching out to people who might actually be outside the echo chamber.
sentences.zh: 而不是去接触那些可能在回声室之外的人。

sentences.en: I love being a Red Sox fan.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢当红袜队的球迷。

sentences.en: And, you know, as I say in the book, I live right near Fenway Park.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如我在书中所说，我就住在芬威球场附近。

sentences.en: I've gone to Fenway Park and taken my children there.
sentences.zh: 我去过芬威球场，也带我的孩子们去过那里。

sentences.en: And the whole, you know, the whole park at Fenway will chant Yankees suck, Yankees suck over and over again.
sentences.zh: 整个芬威球场的观众都会一遍又一遍地高喊“洋基队烂透了，洋基队烂透了”。

sentences.en: They've done it for decades now.
sentences.zh: 他们几十年来一直这样做。

sentences.en: And it's all kind of a joke because the stakes are low.
sentences.zh: 这完全是个玩笑，因为赌注很低。

sentences.en: We don't really hate those people who are the Yankees fans or the Yankees players.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是真的憎恨那些洋基队的球迷或球员。

sentences.en: It's a game and it's fun to be part of it for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这只是一场游戏，对很多人来说，参与其中很有趣。

sentences.en: So what explains the fact that in politics people don't think of it as being fun?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何解释在政治上人们不认为这很有趣呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if you're a Democrat and you think Republicans are terrible or you're a Republican and you think Democrats are terrible, you don't think of it as a game.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你是民主党人，认为共和党人很糟糕，或者你是共和党人，认为民主党人很糟糕，你不会把它当作游戏。

sentences.en: You think of it as being deadly serious.
sentences.zh: 你会认为这是极其严肃的事情。
这也是政治票友行为吗？

sentences.en: What's political hobbyism is not whether you think it's deadly serious or not.
sentences.zh: 政治票友行为的关键不在于你是否认为它极其严肃。

sentences.en: It's whether the emotion is the end in itself or a means to an end.
sentences.zh: 而在于这种情感本身是目的，还是达到目的的手段。

sentences.en: So in shortcut politics, in hobbyism, emotion is the goal.
sentences.zh: 所以，在快餐式政治中，在票友行为中，情感就是目标。

sentences.en: It makes you feel connected to something without doing anything yourself.
sentences.zh: 它让你感觉自己与某事相连，而无需自己做任何事情。

sentences.en: It makes me feel I am part of this emotional high or I am part of this sad point, this low point, even though I'm not doing anything.
sentences.zh: 它让我觉得我参与了这种情感高潮，或者我参与了这种悲伤的低谷，尽管我什么都没做。

sentences.en: But the emotion is the connection.
And of course, we have a whole media apparatus and social media apparatus to make us feel those emotions.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们有一整套媒体机构和社交媒体机构来让我们感受到这些情绪。

sentences.en: But in real politics, anger, righteous anger and emotion are something you leverage into action.
sentences.zh: 但在真正的政治中，愤怒、正义的愤怒和情感是你转化为行动的筹码。

sentences.en: If there's no second step there, you might feel like you're feeling political and partisan thoughts, but you're not channeling them effectively into anything else.
sentences.zh: 如果没有第二步，你可能觉得自己有政治和党派思想，但你并没有有效地将它们引导到其他任何事情上。

sentences.en: So I want to examine your larger evidence for these claiMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我想检验一下你这些主张的更广泛证据。

sentences.en: And I want to start with a revealing story you tell about two elections in your home state of Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我想从你讲述的关于你家乡马萨诸塞州两次选举的一个发人深省的故事开始。

sentences.en: The first was in 2008, and it featured Barack Obama running for president.
sentences.zh: 第一次是在 2008 年，当时 Barack Obama 正在竞选总统。

sentences.en: And the second, 14 months later, featured a special election for a Senate seat that had big implications for the balance of power in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 第二场是在14个月后，当时举行了一场参议院席位的特别选举，这对参议院的权力平衡有着重大影响。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened in those two races.
sentences.zh: 告诉我那两场竞选发生了什么。
